bioghist.head: The Living Theatre
bioghist.p: The Living Theatre was founded in 1947 by Julian Beck and Judith Malina in New York City. The company performed politically charged plays commenting on war, Wall Street, and income inequality even being arrested during some of their public performances. The group produced experimental and little-known plays by writers including Gertrude Stein, William Carlos Williams, and John Ashbery. In 1961, the company toured Europe with one of its biggest successes, "The Connection" and other plays including Paradise Now and The Legacy of Cain . The Living Theatre left New York in 1964 after failing to pay $23,000 in back taxes. Malina and Beck represented themselves in the trial. The theatre company focused on avant garde productions including The Connection and The Brig . Theatre productions often broke the fourth wall and included audience participation. Theatre company members were also arrested for various acts of civil disobedience. The theatre company performed all over the world in public and unique spaces. The theatre returned to New York City in the 1980s. After Julian Beck's death in 1985, Hanon Reznikov was named codirector. Reznikov died in 2008 and Malina in 2015. The Living Theatre continues with artistic director Brad Burgess to conduct workshops and perform in the United States and abroad.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Judith Malina was a prolific diarist and kept an almost daily diary for over 70 years, documenting both her personal and professional lives in great detail. Malina wrote about daily events in her diaries and excluded almost no details. She comments on her physical and mental state, her sexual activities, and her family history. She writes about conversations, feelings, relationships, and events both in her personal life and in the wider world. Malina also wrote about her family, including her parents, her life with Julian Beck, her husband from 1947 until his death in 1985 and co-creator of The Living Theatre, her children, as well as her life with Hanon Reznikov, co-director of The Living Theatre who she married in 1988.

The diaries are a comprehensive look into a life full of teaching, directing, acting, research, and activism. They track the formation of The Living Theatre and its growth and performances over time. Malina's diaries portray her desire to form the theatre, the theatre's triumphs and challenges over the years, and its transition into the 21st century. They include details about productions, performances, rehearsing, and writing. The diaries also offer a glimpse into the lives of the artists, actors, writers, and directors that were colleagues, friends, collaborators, and students of Malina's.

Judith Malina's diaries are mostly handwritten in notebooks of various sizes, and some include small photographs, ephemera, and portions of correspondence or conversations written in Malina's hand. Most of the diaries were identified as being written in New York City, but other locations where Malina traveled to, lived in, and worked in include Brazil, France, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, and Greece. Grove Press published her diaries in one volume entitled The Diaries of Judith Malina, 1947-1957 in 1984. In addition to the diaries, the subseries includes appointment calendars and notebooks in which Malina kept her notes about different productions and research topics.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: In the subseries inventory, diaries are titled according to the location at which they were written. Diaries for which a location was not specified are titled, "Diary with unspecified location."

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Judith Malina was born in Kiel, Germany on June 4, 1926. In 1929, her family emigrated to New York City. She met her future husband and collaborator, Julian Beck in 1943. In 1945, Malina made her acting debut, studying at the New School for Social Research, studying with Erwin Piscator. She married Julian Beck in 1948. Their son, Garrick Beck, was born in 1949. Her daughter Isha was born in 1967. Together in 1947, they founded The Living Theatre, an alternative theater company which was based in New York City. She created, directed, and acted in the company's plays including Antigone , Frankenstein , and Paradise Now . She also taught at New York University and Columbia University. Malina appeared in film and television, including The Sopranos , The Addams Family , and Dog Day Afternoon . Along with articles and monographs, she published her early diaries and a memoir of her theatre training under Erwin Piscator, The Piscator Notebook and a book of poetry, Poems of a Wandering Jewess . In 1988, Malina married Hanon Reznikov, a writer, director, actor in the Living Theatre, who became codirector of the company after Julian Beck's death. Reznikov died in 2008. Malina died on April 10, 2015.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Julian Beck was born on May 31, 1925, in Washington Heights, Manhattan. He attended Yale University and dropped out to pursue art and writing. He established The Living Theatre with his wife, Judith Malina, in 1947. Beck also acted outside of the theatre, appearing in films including The Poltergeist II and Cotton Club and an episode of Miami Vice. He published two non-fiction books, The Life of the Theatre and Theandric, along with several volumes of poetry. Beck was diagnosed with stomach cancer in 1983 and died on September 14, 1985.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The subseries documents the life and work of Julian Beck, particularly his creative process, writings, and acting career. Beck's journals and notebooks provide a detailed account of his daily life and work. The subseries also contains drafts, notes, research files, and correspondence relating to Beck's writings, including works he wrote collaboratively with his wife Judith Malina and other members of The Living Theatre. Also present are scripts, correspondence, and production files relating to Beck's career in theatre, film, and television; Beck's literary and personal correspondence; papers relating to his painting and art career; the contents of his desk and office at the time of his death; and personal papers, including school papers, financial records, medical records, and Beck's collection of ephemera, printed material, and clippings.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Hanon Reznikov (1950-2008) was a performer, director, and co-managing director of The Living Theatre, particularly after the death of Julian Beck in 1985.

Reznikov was born in Brooklyn as Howard Reznik. As an adult he changed his name to Hanon Reznikov. He enrolled at Yale University (YC 1972) where he first encountered The Living Theatre as an undergraduate student. In 1977 he joined the company as a performer. During his time with The Living Theatre he also wrote and produced plays, traveled with the company, and assisted in shaping the Theatre.

In 1985, after the death of Julian Beck, Reznikov took over the position of co-artistic director in partnership with Judith Malina. In 1988 he married Malina and remained married to her until he died in 2008 from pneumonia following a stroke.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries contains the professional and personal papers created and collected by Hanon Reznikov (1950-2008), co-director of The Living Theatre and Judith Malina's husband after the death of Julian Beck. The materials include documents that reflect Reznikov's time with The Living Theatre, beginning early in his tenure with the company, up to his death in 2008.

Materials in this subseries include diaries, notebooks, address and datebooks, production materials, theatre administrative materials, financial documents, personal and professional correspondence, and writings by Reznikov as well as others. There are also personal documents, such as marriage and death certificates. The diaries and notebooks provide insight to Reznikov's artistic decisions regarding touring, productions, and performance. The Writings grouping, which contains material written both by Reznikov and by other writers, expands these insights to include his thoughts and views that did not end up in productions.

The production materials range from scripts, including annotated ones, set and technical breakdowns, and promotional materials for various The Living Theatre productions in which Reznikov participated. Financial documents include personal tax returns, Stage Actors Guild pay stubs and pension stubs, and paycheck records for The Living Theatre. This records the financial realities of both the theatre company as well as Reznikov and Malina during their marriage. Also contained in these materials are records detailing the day-to-day administration of The Living Theatre, including marketing, financial, and tour records.

The correspondence in this series is primarily personal and includes correspondence between Reznikov and friends and family. There is some correspondence from Reznikov's time at Yale, which records Reznikov's early experiences with theatre at Yale. Professional correspondence primarily discusses The Living Theatre and features an assortment of correspondents.

Personal material in this series consists of records that deal with Reznikov's day to day life outside of the theatre, including government records, death certificates, real estate research, and some family material.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Living Theatre was founded in 1947 by Julian Beck and Judith Malina in New York City. The company performed politically charged plays commenting on war, Wall Street, and income inequality even being arrested during some of their public performances. The group produced experimental and little-known plays by writers including Gertrude Stein, William Carlos Williams, and John Ashbery. In 1961, the company toured Europe with one of its biggest successes, "The Connection" and other plays including "Paradise Now" and "The Legacy of Cain". The Living Theatre left New York in 1964 after failing to pay $23,000 in back taxes. Malina and Beck represented themselves in the trial. The theatre company focused on avant garde productions including "The Connection" and "The Brig". Theatre productions often broke the fourth wall and included audience participation. Theatre company members were also arrested for various acts of civil disobedience. The theatre company performed all over the world in public and unique spaces. The theatre returned to New York City in the 1980s. After Julian Beck's death in 1985, Hanon Reznikov was named codirector. Reznikov died in 2008 and Malina in 2015. The Living Theatre continues with artistic director Brad Burgess to conduct workshops and perform in the United States and abroad.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The subseries documents the period when the Living Theatre lived and worked in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania from November 1974 through May 1975. As part of the "Pittsburgh campaign," the company conducted research about Pittsburgh, became involved in a variety of community organizations, and staged a series of public performances that formed part of The Legacy of Cain cycle of plays. The campaign was intended to engage "cells," or specific segments of the population, such as young people and industrial workers. The subseries contains research materials, clippings, photographs, maps, and notes the company used when planning the campaign. It also contains production materials, including rehearsal notes, correspondence, schedules, fliers, programs, receipt, and a scrapbook.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Photograph subseries primarily contains photographs and slides from productions and performances by the Living Theatre. Some of these photographs contain information on the photographer, performers, or the venue or theatre in which the production was performed. Slides are primarily of productions, not promotional images. Many photographs are of tour productions, both in the United States and abroad. Photographs of specific productions on tour are listed under the production's name. Photographs that primarily document workshops, tour events, tour social events, or festivals, are listed under the Tour heading.

Also present are photographs of the company, individuals in the company, and promotional photographs. These include headshots of Julian Beck, Judith Malina, and Hanon Reznikov. These photographs include professional and personal materials, including rehearsals, events, parties, and other social and professional events. However, the personal and social photographs are all linked to the Living Theatre, recording events that would have included members of the company outside of Malina, Beck, or Reznikov.

There are some photographs of theatre buildings, including the theater used by the Living Theatre on 14th Street, in New York City, New York, rehearsal and theater layouts, and advertising for programs.

scopecontent.p: The subseries General Strike for Peace refer to materials related to the General Strike for Peace movement for which Judith Malina and Julian Beck were organizers. The subseries also includes returned outreach letters that were never opened due to inaccurate mailing addresses. The last box contains a rolodex of organizational contacts.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Company Members subseries contains the records of five members of The Living Theatre who served in various functions, primarily as actors. Materials include: personal diaries and journals detailing their time with The Living Theatre; scripts (many original copies annotated with the actor's notes); correspondence; personal and professional writings; photographs of Living Theatre productions; advertisements and publicity materials for plays and performances; and organizational records.

As of 2025, Brad Burgess is the current artistic director of The Living Theatre. He previously served as Associate Artistic Director, working alongside Judith Malina until her death in 2015. The materials in this grouping include business and operational records for the Living Theatre, and scripts, promotional materials, and cast information regarding Living Theatre productions from the early 2000s to present day.

Leroy "Rain" House performed in many Living Theatre productions from the 1960s through the 1990s. The materials in this grouping include approx. 100 personal and professional notebooks documenting his time with The Living Theatre, scripts, photographs of Living Theatre productions as well as personal photographs of Rain House and family.

Craig Peritz joined The Living Theatre in 1997 and was involved with productions both in the United States and in Europe. Materials in this grouping consist mainly of personal journals and writings by Peritz during his time with The Living Theatre.

Luke Theodore (1934-1991) joined The Living Theatre in 1963 and performed in many productions, including The Brig (1963), Maids (1965), Antigone (1967), and Paradise Now (1968). Materials in this grouping include original scripts, personal and professional dairies, writings, photographs of Living Theatre productions, and personal and professional correspondence, in particular correspondence with actress and singer Tally Brown, a prominent figure in the New York City avant-garde and underground performing arts world of the 1960s.

Ilion Troya first joined The Living Theatre in 1971 after seeing a performance in Rio Claro, Brazil. He continues to be involved with The Living Theatre through the present day, in various capacities including performer, designer, writer, translator, and serving on the International Board of The Living Theatre. Materials in this grouping consist primarily of scripts, notebooks, and personal writings by Troya documenting Living Theatre productions in the United States and touring abroad. Also of note is a diary of Judith Malina and Julian Beck written in Switzerland in 1985 and edited by Troya, and writings by Troya containing personal remembrances of Julian Beck.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The subseries is arranged into five groupings: I. Burgess, Brad, papers, II. House, Rain, papers, III. Peritz, Craig, papers, IV. Theodore, Luke, papers, V. Troya, Ilion, papers. Materials arranged alphabetically within each grouping.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Living Theater Company and Non-Company Members papers reveal the interpersonal relationships among cast members, friends, and acquaintances of Judith Malina and Julian Beck. This collection explores the emotional experiences of company members through their personal notebooks and correspondence. T

This subseries includes materials belonging to Carl Einhorn, a company member and love interest of Judith Malina. These records provide insight into the emotional and romantic partnership between Einhorn and Malina. Among the materials are playing cards and intimate drawings sent between one another as a symbol of love. There is one letter sent to Isha Manna Beck, the daughter of Malina and reported child of Einhorn.

This collection contains personal papers of Lester Schwartz, a lover of both Judith Malina and Julian Beck. His correspondence depicts a vulnerable exchange with the theater founders. The presence of a note from Malina and Beck's child, Gerrick Beck, "Garry", highlights the intertwined nature of professional and personal lives in the theater.
Present in the collection are personal notebooks and poetry by the actress Jenny Hecht. Her papers reveal her expereinces with The Living Theater in the 1960s.

The collection includes personal papers from various other company members, notably Eduardo Silva and Parvaneh Tokamani, as well as several notebooks by unidentified authors. Additionally, there are records from non-company members who were acquaintances of Judith Malina and Julian Beck.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series contains materials written about The Living Theatre by scholars, writers, and students who were interested in The Living Theatre. The series contains manuscripts sent to Judith Malina, Julian Beck, and Hanon Reznikov at different stages of the creative process, often at the writers' request for commentary, proofreading, and editing. It includes galleys, complete and incomplete drafts of novels, plays, film scripts, poems and poetic drama pieces, academic theses, letters accompanying the manuscripts, and unidentified drafts with unknown authorship.

The thematic content of this series is as wide-ranging as the types of manuscript material found in it. It includes heavily annotated drafts of nonfiction work written by critic and historian of the Beat Generation, John Tytell. It also features manuscripts from other writers associated with the Beat movement, like Claude Pelieu and Mark Sacharoff whose incomplete autobiographical essay drafts talk about the theatre's connection with the Beat movement and its central figures. Other works of nonfiction come in the form of graduate theses, written in English, French and Italian, and delving into the theatre's history, productions, travels, and other activities in Europe between 1960s-80s, the United States, and beyond. Other writers represented in the series include Norman McAfee, Andrea Dworkin, Jean Cocteau, Berolt Brecht, Arnold Weinstein, Robert Kramer, Karen Malpede, and Leon Katz, among others.
